units.text: To register a moped (limited use motorcycle) in New York, you must have a driver license and register it to drive on streets and highways.
units.reason: The context states: 'You must have a driver license and register your moped to drive it on streets and highways.'

units.text: You cannot operate it on a sidewalk.
units.reason: The context states: 'You can never operate a moped down a sidewalk.'

units.text: Bring to the DMV: a completed Registration/Title Application (MV-82), proof of ownership, proof of identity and age (you must be at least 16), proof of insurance if required, and payment for fees and sales tax.
units.reason: The context lists these items and states 'You must be at least 16 years old to register a vehicle in New York'.

units.text: The class (A, B, or C) is determined by top speed, and only certified models can be registered.
units.reason: The context states: 'The DMV classifies a moped as a Class A, Class B or Class C limited use motorcycle according to its top speed. Only a certified model of limited use motorcycle can get a registration in New York State'.

units.text: For quicker service, make a reservation online before visiting offices in certain counties.
units.reason: The context states: 'For quicker service, make a reservation online before visiting offices in New York City, Westchester, Nassau, Suffolk, Rockland, Onondaga, Monroe or Albany Counties.'
